_comment: First batch covering ce_marking.*, declaration.* and provider.*. Organisation/product means a fact maintained once for an organisation or marketed product and reused across deployments. System means a fact that depends on the particular AI system, its market placement, or its deployment. These are reviewable interpretations; uncertain boundaries are labelled in the rationale.

organisation.ce_marking.affixed: Article 48(3) attaches the mark to the marketed high-risk system or its packaging/documentation. For the same product, the mark is reused across deployments, so this is classified at product level. Uncertain: a change that creates a distinct AI system may need its own mark; the system boundary controls.
organisation.ce_marking.visible_legible_indelible: Article 48(3) requires the physical CE mark to be visible, legible and indelible on the system or, where appropriate, its packaging or accompanying documentation. The policy checks this field only for non-digital systems; digital systems use ce_marking.digital_marking_accessible. For the same marketed product and conformity scope, physical presentation can be reused across deployments. Uncertain: materially different system variants or packaging may need separate marking evidence.
organisation.declaration.drawn_up: Article 47(1) requires a declaration for each high-risk AI system. This is classified at product level as one declaration for the marketed system, not one per deployment. Uncertain: variants that amount to a distinct AI system need a separate declaration.
organisation.declaration.machine_readable: Article 47(1) specifies the accepted form of the declaration. Once prepared for a marketed system, this form is reused across that system's deployments.
organisation.provider.ce_marking_affixed: This is the provider-side version of ce_marking.affixed. Article 16(h) and Article 48 attach the mark to the marketed system or its packaging, so I classify it at product level. Uncertain: a materially different system may require a separate mark.
organisation.provider.corrective_action_process: Article 20 requires corrective action for a non-conforming system, while this field asks whether the provider has a process for taking that action. The process can be maintained once across the provider's systems. Uncertain: the actions and evidence remain system-specific.
organisation.provider.declaration_of_conformity_drawn: Article 16(g) and Article 47 require a declaration for each high-risk AI system. This is classified at product level as one declaration for the marketed system, not for each deployment. Uncertain: a product variant that is a distinct AI system needs its own declaration.
organisation.provider.identification_on_system_or_pac: Article 16(b) requires the provider's name and contact address on the system, packaging, or accompanying documentation. The identity is shared across the provider's products, while the label is carried with each marketed product. Uncertain: the field may be intended to record the placement for each individual system.
organisation.provider.quality_management_system: Article 17(1) requires the provider to maintain a documented quality management system covering its compliance processes. This is an organisation-level system that can cover multiple AI products.

system.ce_marking.digital_marking_accessible: Article 48(2) requires a digital CE mark for a high-risk AI system provided digitally, if it can be accessed through that system's interface or another accessible electronic means. The interface and delivery form are system-specific.
system.ce_marking.notified_body_involved: Whether a notified body was involved depends on the conformity assessment for the particular high-risk AI system under Article 43 and Article 48(4).
system.ce_marking.notified_body_number_displaye: Article 48(4) requires the identification number of the notified body responsible for the particular system's conformity assessment, so the answer can differ by system.
system.declaration.annex_v_content_complete: Article 47(2) requires the declaration to contain the information in Annex V and identify the high-risk AI system. Its completeness therefore depends on that system's declaration.
system.declaration.retained_ten_years: Article 47(1) starts the ten-year retention period when the particular system is placed on the market or put into service. Each system can have a different start date and record.
system.declaration.translated_for_market: Article 47(2) requires the declaration to be translated into a language easily understood by competent authorities in the Member States where this particular system is placed on the market or made available. This is classified per system because the answer depends on that system's market scope; translations can be reused only across deployments of the same system within the same Member State scope.
system.provider.accessibility_requirements_met: Article 16(l) makes accessibility compliance an obligation for the high-risk AI system. The answer depends on that system's design and interfaces.
system.provider.conformity_assessment_completed: Article 16(f) and Article 43 require the relevant conformity assessment before the particular high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service.
system.provider.logs_kept: Article 16(e) and Article 19 concern logs automatically generated by a particular system and retained only to the extent they are under the provider's control.
system.provider.registered_in_eu_database: Article 16(i) refers to Article 49(1): before market placement or putting into service, the provider or, where applicable, its authorised representative must register themselves and the system for Annex III high-risk systems except those in point 2 of Annex III. Article 49(5) instead requires point 2 systems to be registered nationally. This is classified per system because each record identifies a particular system. Uncertain: the field combines the actor's registration with the system's registration and does not express the national registration route for point 2 systems.
system.provider.technical_documentation_kept: Article 16(d) and Article 18 require the technical documentation for each high-risk AI system to be retained for ten years from that system's placement on the market or putting into service.
